library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Liu et al. (2019) model the deuterium oxide (D2O) dose-to-the-mother (DTM)
technique, which is used to tell whether an infant is exclusively breastfed.
The mother drinks about 30 g of D2O; it mixes into her body water, and some of
it reaches her infant through breast milk. Saliva enrichment of both is then
measured over 14 days. The model is two linked one-compartment models (paper
Fig. 1): the mother loses D2O at a total rate constant `kmm`, part of which is
the lactation clearance `CLmb` into the infant, and the infant loses it through
its own water clearance `CLbo`. The infant's volume of distribution is not
estimated; it is computed from infant weight and grows with the infant. The
quantity the paper is after is `Rs`, the infant's water intake from sources
other than breast milk, which follows from `CLmb` and `CLbo` by a water mass
balance (paper Appendix 1, reproduced below).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2019_deuterium"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2019_deuterium"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-018-9613-x> (open access; the seven
  Electronic Supplementary Materials include the Stan code (ESM 4), the
  population parameters (ESM 6, Table S6.1) and the individual posterior means
  (ESM 5)).

# Population

113 exclusively breastfeeding mother-infant pairs from Sumedang, West Java,
Indonesia (121 recruited; 7 removed as non-exclusively breastfed on home
observation and 1 as biologically implausible), giving 1500 paired saliva
observations (paper Results, Data; Table 1). Mothers were 25 years old (range
16-42) and weighed 53.1 kg (34.5-93.1). Infants were singleton, full-term and
healthy, 3.3 months old (2.0-5.4), 54 male and 59 female, and weighed 5.9 kg
(3.9-8.4) at the start and 6.2 kg (4.3-8.5) at the end of the 14-day protocol.
Each mother received about 30 g of D2O orally (30.0-30.2 g); saliva was sampled
from both before the dose and on days 1, 2, 5, 6, 13 and 14.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: `d/dt(central) = -kmm * central`; `d/dt(infant_central) = kmb * central - kbo * infant_central` | -- | Eqs. 3-4; Fig. 1 |
| `kmb = CLmb / Vm`, `kbo = CLbo / Vb` | -- | Eqs. 1-2 |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / Vm`, `Cinfant = 1000 * infant_central / Vb` (g to mg/L) | -- | ESM 4 Stan code `amt*1000/Vm` |
| `lvc` (Vm at maternal weight 70 kg) | 3.49 (32.8 L) | Eq. 16 |
| `lkel` (kmm) | -2.2277 (0.108 1/day) | Table S6.1 mean 0.109 1/day with BSV 15.0%, `log(0.109) - 0.15^2/2` |
| `lcl_milk` (CLmb) | -0.33 (0.719 L/day) | ESM 7, `log(CLmb) ~ N(-0.33, 0.20)` |
| `lcl_infant` (CLbo at infant weight 5 kg) | -0.16 (0.852 L/day) | Eq. 17 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.62 | Eq. 16; Stan `pow(MWT[i]/70, theta[1])` |
| `e_wt_infant_cl_infant` | 0.17 | Eq. 17; Stan `pow(BWT[i]/5, theta[2])` |
| `etalvc` variance | 0.070^2 | Table S6.1 BSV 7.0%; Eq. 16 SD 0.07 |
| `etalkel` variance | 0.150^2 | Table S6.1 BSV 15.0% |
| `etalcl_milk`, `etalcl_infant` variances | 0.201^2, 0.171^2 | Table S6.1 BSV 20.1%, 17.1%; ESM 7 SDs 0.20, 0.17 |
| `etalcl_milk`-`etalcl_infant` correlation | 0.99 | ESM 7, note 2 |
| Infant volume `Vb = 1.041 * exp(-0.427 + 0.963 * log(WT_INFANT))` | -- | Eqs. A1.9-A1.10; Stan `Vb_b` |
| Residual error: combined, one sigma pair for mother and infant | not reported, held at 0 | Eq. 7; Stan `sigma` |
| `Rs` mass balance (vignette only) | -- | Eqs. A1.3-A1.13; Stan `Rs` |

# Typical values against the published population table

Table S6.1 prints *arithmetic* population means. For a log-normal parameter
that mean is `exp(mu + omega^2 / 2)`, so the packaged log-scale typical values
and variances must reproduce it. Three of the four `mu` values are printed in
the paper (Eqs. 16-17, ESM 7), which makes this a check of the reading of
"BSV %" as the log-scale SD; `kmm` was back-solved from the same relationship,
so for it the check is only arithmetic.

```{r typical-values}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Liu_2019_deuterium"))
ini_df <- mod$iniDf
th <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)
om <- function(eta) th[[eta]]

tv_check <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("Vm (L)", "kmm (1/day)", "CLmb (L/day)", "CLbo (L/day)"),
  mu = c(th[["lvc"]], th[["lkel"]], th[["lcl_milk"]], th[["lcl_infant"]]),
  omega2 = c(om("etalvc"), om("etalkel"), om("etalcl_milk"), om("etalcl_infant")),
  published_mean = c(32.86, 0.109, 0.733, 0.864)
) |>
  mutate(
    median = exp(mu),
    model_mean = exp(mu + omega2 / 2),
    pct_diff = 100 * (model_mean / published_mean - 1)
  )
knitr::kable(
  tv_check |>
    select(parameter, median, model_mean, published_mean, pct_diff) |>
    rename(
      "Parameter" = parameter,
      "exp(mu)" = median,
      "Model arithmetic mean" = model_mean,
      "Table S6.1 mean" = published_mean,
      "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 3
)
# The printed mu values carry two decimals, i.e. +/- 0.005 on the log scale,
# so agreement to within 0.6% is all the rounding allows.
stopifnot(all(abs(tv_check$pct_diff) < 0.6))
```

ESM 5 lists each pair's posterior mean of these four parameters *before* the
covariate effects are applied (`exp(phi)` in the Stan code; the maternal
volumes centre on 32.8 L although the mothers weighed 53 kg). Their geometric
means are therefore a second, independent estimate of `exp(mu)`. Computed from
the 113 rows of ESM 5, they are 32.85 L, 0.1071 1/day, 0.7205 L/day and
0.8494 L/day, and the correlation between the individual `log(CLmb)` and
`log(CLbo)` is 0.997.

```{r esm5-check}
esm5_geomean <- c(32.85, 0.1071, 0.7205, 0.8494)
stopifnot(all(abs(log(tv_check$median / esm5_geomean)) < 0.01))
```

# Structural check: ODE against the authors' closed form

The Stan code does not integrate ODEs; it evaluates the analytic solution of
Eqs. 3-4 (paper Eqs. 5-6) with the infant volume `Vb` taken at each
observation time. That is exact while the infant's weight is constant, and a
frozen-coefficient approximation while it grows. The packaged model integrates
the mass-balanced ODEs with a time-varying `Vb`, so for a constant infant
weight the two must agree to integrator precision and for a growing infant
they should differ slightly.

```{r closed-form}
stan_closed_form <- function(time, dose, mwt, wt_infant, bwt, p) {
  vm <- exp(p[["lvc"]]) * (mwt / 70)^p[["e_wt_vc"]]
  kmm <- exp(p[["lkel"]])
  clmb <- exp(p[["lcl_milk"]])
  clbo <- exp(p[["lcl_infant"]]) * (bwt / 5)^p[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]]
  vb <- 1.041 * exp(-0.427 + 0.963 * log(wt_infant))
  data.frame(
    time = time,
    Cc = dose * 1000 / vm * exp(-kmm * time),
    Cinfant = dose * 1000 / vm * clmb / (vb * (kmm - clbo / vb)) *
      (exp(-clbo / vb * time) - exp(-kmm * time))
  )
}

typical_events <- function(wt_start, wt_end, t_end = 14, dt = 0.125) {
  obs_t <- seq(0, t_end, by = dt)
  rbind(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 30, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = obs_t, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    mutate(WT = 53.1, WT_INFANT = wt_start + (wt_end - wt_start) * time / t_end)
}

mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Constant infant weight: the closed form is exact.
ev_const <- typical_events(6.05, 6.05)
sim_const <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_const, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
                             returnType = "data.frame")
cf_const <- stan_closed_form(sim_const$time, 30, 53.1, 6.05, 6.05, th)
late <- sim_const$time >= 0.5
err_const <- max(abs(c(sim_const$Cc[late] / cf_const$Cc[late] - 1,
                       sim_const$Cinfant[late] / cf_const$Cinfant[late] - 1)))
err_const
stopifnot(err_const < 1e-6)

# Typical growth, 5.9 -> 6.2 kg over 14 days (Table 1 medians); the paper's
# clearance covariate is the study-average weight, 6.05 kg.
ev_grow <- typical_events(5.9, 6.2)
sim_grow <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_grow, covsInterpolation = "linear",
                            returnType = "data.frame")
cf_grow <- stan_closed_form(sim_grow$time, 30, 53.1,
                            5.9 + 0.3 * sim_grow$time / 14, 6.05, th)
dev_grow <- (sim_grow$Cinfant / cf_grow$Cinfant - 1)[sim_grow$time >= 1]
range(100 * dev_grow)
stopifnot(max(abs(dev_grow)) < 0.03)
```

For a typical infant growing 0.3 kg over the study the mass-balanced ODE
gives infant enrichment up to about 1.7% below the authors' frozen-volume
form at day 14; the maternal profile is identical.

# Replicating Figure 2

Figure 2 of the paper shows individual fits for four pairs. The maternal
profile starts near 1000-1100 mg/L and falls monoexponentially, the infant's
rises to a peak of about 350-550 mg/L around days 5-6, and the two curves
cross between about day 8 and day 12, after which the infant is the more
enriched. The figure below shows the same profiles for the typical pair and
the 95% between-subject band of a 200-pair virtual cohort.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190101)
n_pairs <- 200

# Reject-and-redraw inside the Table 1 ranges; a clamp would pile mass on
# the boundaries.
draw_lnorm <- function(n, median, sdlog, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- exp(rnorm(n, log(median), sdlog))
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}
pairs <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_pairs),
  WT = draw_lnorm(n_pairs, 53.1, 0.20, 34.5, 93.1),
  wt_start = draw_lnorm(n_pairs, 5.9, 0.15, 3.9, 8.4)
) |>
  mutate(wt_end = wt_start + 0.3)

obs_t <- seq(0, 14, by = 0.25)
ev_cohort <- bind_rows(
  pairs |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 30, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::crossing(pairs, time = obs_t) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(WT_INFANT = wt_start + (wt_end - wt_start) * time / 14) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, WT, WT_INFANT)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cohort, covsInterpolation = "linear",
                       returnType = "data.frame")

# The model has no residual error (not reported), so these are the
# between-subject spreads of the true saliva enrichment.
stopifnot(all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cc)), all(sim$Cinfant >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cinfant)))
```

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Replicates the shape of Figure 2 of Liu 2019: maternal (upper at day 0) and infant (lower at day 0) saliva D2O enrichment after a 30 g oral dose to the mother. Lines: typical pair (maternal weight 53.1 kg, infant 5.9 to 6.2 kg); band: 2.5th-97.5th percentiles of 200 simulated pairs."}
band <- sim |>
  select(id, time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(member, time) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(conc, 0.025), hi = quantile(conc, 0.975), .groups = "drop")
typ <- sim_grow |>
  select(time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc")
member_lab <- c(Cc = "Mother", Cinfant = "Infant")

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(time, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = member), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = typ, aes(time, conc, colour = member), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = member_lab) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = member_lab) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "D2O concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig2-checks}
typ_w <- sim_grow
c0 <- typ_w$Cc[typ_w$time == 0]
t_peak_inf <- typ_w$time[which.max(typ_w$Cinfant)]
c_peak_inf <- max(typ_w$Cinfant)
t_cross <- typ_w$time[which(typ_w$time > 1 & typ_w$Cinfant >= typ_w$Cc)[1]]
c(c0 = c0, t_peak_infant = t_peak_inf, c_peak_infant = c_peak_inf, t_cross = t_cross)
stopifnot(
  c0 > 1000, c0 < 1150,
  t_peak_inf >= 5, t_peak_inf <= 7,
  c_peak_inf > 350, c_peak_inf < 550,
  t_cross >= 8, t_cross <= 12
)
```

The typical pair starts at `r round(c0)` mg/L, the infant peaks at
`r round(c_peak_inf)` mg/L on day `r t_peak_inf`, and the curves cross on
day `r t_cross`, all inside the range of the four pairs in Figure 2.

# Non-compartmental analysis

The paper reports no NCA, so the PKNCA results are checked against the
model's own closed forms for the typical pair: for the mother `t1/2 = log(2) /
kmm` and `AUC0-inf = 1000 * Dose / (Vm * kmm)`; for an infant of constant
weight every gram that leaves the mother through milk (`Dose * CLmb /
(Vm * kmm)`) is eventually cleared by `CLbo`, so `AUC0-inf = 1000 * Dose *
CLmb / (Vm * kmm * CLbo)`. The typical pair is followed for 120 days so that
the infant's terminal phase, which runs at the slower maternal rate, is
well established.

```{r nca-typical}
ev_long <- typical_events(6.05, 6.05, t_end = 120, dt = 0.25)
sim_long <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_long, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
                            returnType = "data.frame")
# A single-subject solve returns no id column.
conc_long <- sim_long |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0))
dose_long <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, dose = 30,
                        member = c("Cc", "Cinfant"))
nca_long <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_long, conc ~ time | member + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_long, dose ~ time | member + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
res_long <- as.data.frame(nca_long$result)

vm_t <- exp(th[["lvc"]]) * (53.1 / 70)^th[["e_wt_vc"]]
kmm_t <- exp(th[["lkel"]])
clmb_t <- exp(th[["lcl_milk"]])
clbo_t <- exp(th[["lcl_infant"]]) * (6.05 / 5)^th[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]]
expected <- data.frame(
  member = c("Cc", "Cc", "Cinfant", "Cinfant"),
  PPTESTCD = c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  expected = c(30000 / (vm_t * kmm_t), log(2) / kmm_t,
               30000 * clmb_t / (vm_t * kmm_t * clbo_t), log(2) / kmm_t)
)
nca_cmp <- res_long |>
  inner_join(expected, by = c("member", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / expected - 1))
knitr::kable(
  nca_cmp |>
    mutate(member = member_lab[member]) |>
    select(member, PPTESTCD, PPORRES, expected, pct_diff) |>
    rename("Dyad member" = member, "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
           "PKNCA" = PPORRES, "Closed form" = expected, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff),
  digits = 3
)
# Deterministic typical-pair solve. Measured: AUCs within 0.02%; the infant
# half-life 0.8% long because PKNCA's automatic point selection reaches back
# to where the infant's faster disposition phase has not fully decayed.
stopifnot(all(abs(nca_cmp$pct_diff) < 2))
```

For the virtual cohort over the 14-day protocol, the NCA by dyad member is:

```{r nca-cohort}
conc_cohort <- sim |>
  select(id, time, Cc, Cinfant) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cinfant), names_to = "member", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0))
dose_cohort <- tidyr::crossing(id = pairs$id, member = c("Cc", "Cinfant")) |>
  mutate(time = 0, dose = 30)
nca_cohort <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_cohort, conc ~ time | member + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_cohort, dose ~ time | member + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 14, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
nca_sum <- as.data.frame(nca_cohort$result) |>
  group_by(member, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), p05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
            p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(member = member_lab[member])
knitr::kable(
  nca_sum |>
    rename("Dyad member" = member, "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
           "Median" = median, "5th percentile" = p05, "95th percentile" = p95),
  digits = 2
)
```

# Water intake from non-milk sources (Rs)

Appendix 1 of the paper turns the two clearances into the infant's intake of
water from sources other than breast milk. With all quantities in L/day,

* breast-milk intake `M = CLmb / 0.889` (free water 88.9% of milk, Eq. A1.4);
* water from oxidising the milk's protein, fat and lactose `Rm = 0.07733 * M`
  (Eq. A1.7);
* infant water output corrected for isotope fractionation `Rcbo = CLbo /
  0.9906` (Eq. A1.12);
* water retained for growth `Rg = (TBW_end - TBW_start) / 14` (Eq. A1.8);
* water absorbed from the atmosphere `Ra = 0.063 * (Rcbo + Rg)` (Eq. A1.13);

and `Rs = Rcbo + Rg - CLmb - Rm - Ra` (Eq. A1.3), reported in g/day. In the
Stan code `CLbo` here is evaluated at the infant's average study weight; with
linear growth that is the weight at day 7, which is when `cl_infant` is read
below. The paper samples the milk-composition, fractionation and atmospheric
constants from priors; here they are held at their means.

```{r rs}
tbw <- function(wt) exp(-0.427 + 0.963 * log(wt))
rs_calc <- function(cl_milk, cl_infant, wt_start, wt_end, days = 14) {
  m_milk <- cl_milk / 0.889
  rm <- 0.07733 * m_milk
  rcbo <- cl_infant / 0.9906
  rg <- (tbw(wt_end) - tbw(wt_start)) / days
  ra <- 0.063 * (rcbo + rg)
  1000 * (rcbo + rg - cl_milk - rm - ra)
}

rs_pairs <- sim |>
  filter(abs(time - 7) < 1e-8) |>
  select(id, cl_milk, cl_infant) |>
  inner_join(pairs, by = "id") |>
  mutate(Rs = rs_calc(cl_milk, cl_infant, wt_start, wt_end))
rs_typ <- rs_calc(exp(th[["lcl_milk"]]), clbo_t, 5.9, 6.2)

# Rs is linear in CLmb and CLbo, so its population mean is the mass balance
# evaluated at the arithmetic-mean clearances exp(mu + omega^2 / 2) -- the
# Table S6.1 quantities -- with no Monte Carlo involved.
mean_clmb <- exp(th[["lcl_milk"]] + om("etalcl_milk") / 2)
mean_clbo5 <- exp(th[["lcl_infant"]] + om("etalcl_infant") / 2)
f_wt <- function(wt) (wt / 5)^th[["e_wt_infant_cl_infant"]]
rs_expected <- rs_calc(mean_clmb, mean_clbo5 * f_wt(6.05), 5.9, 6.2)
# The same mass balance at the arithmetic means of the ESM 5 individual
# posterior means (CLmb 0.7347, CLbo 0.8604 L/day before the weight effect).
rs_esm5 <- rs_calc(0.7347, 0.8604 * f_wt(6.05), 5.9, 6.2)
# Sensitivity of Rs to 0.1 kg of average infant weight.
rs_per_100g <- rs_expected - rs_calc(mean_clmb, mean_clbo5 * f_wt(5.95), 5.8, 6.1)

rs_summary <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Typical pair (exp(mu) clearances)",
    "Population mean, Table S6.1 clearance means",
    "Population mean, ESM 5 posterior-mean clearances",
    "Simulated cohort mean",
    "Simulated cohort SD",
    "Simulated cohort 90th percentile"
  ),
  value = c(rs_typ, rs_expected, rs_esm5, mean(rs_pairs$Rs), sd(rs_pairs$Rs),
            quantile(rs_pairs$Rs, 0.9)),
  published = c(NA, 50.7, 50.7, 50.7, 0.571 * 50.7, NA)
)
knitr::kable(
  rs_summary |>
    rename("Rs (g/day)" = quantity, "This model" = value,
           "Table S6.1" = published),
  digits = 1
)
```

```{r rs-checks}
# Deterministic centre. Rs is the small difference of two 0.99-correlated
# clearances (~0.9 and ~0.8 L/day): 0.001 L/day in CLbo is ~1 g/day of Rs, and
# the paper's own two summaries of CLbo (Table S6.1 0.864, ESM 5 0.8604)
# already differ by 0.0036 L/day. Measured: 59.2 against 50.7.
stopifnot(abs(rs_expected - 50.7) < 12)

# The cohort must agree with the model's own expectation for the cohort's
# weights; 4 Monte-Carlo standard errors.
rs_cohort_expected <- mean(rs_calc(
  mean_clmb, mean_clbo5 * f_wt((pairs$wt_start + pairs$wt_end) / 2),
  pairs$wt_start, pairs$wt_end
))
stopifnot(abs(mean(rs_pairs$Rs) - rs_cohort_expected) <
            4 * sd(rs_pairs$Rs) / sqrt(nrow(rs_pairs)))
```

Table S6.1 gives a population mean `Rs` of 50.7 g/day with 57.1% between-
subject variability. The model's population mean, from the same table's
clearance means, is `r round(rs_expected, 1)` g/day. The gap is a property of
`Rs` rather than of the model: `Rs` is the small difference between the
infant's water turnover and its milk-water intake, two clearances near 0.9 and
0.8 L/day that are 0.99-correlated, so it amplifies their uncertainty roughly
fifteen-fold. Evaluating the same mass balance at the arithmetic means of the
ESM 5 individual posterior clearances instead of the Table S6.1 values already
moves it to `r round(rs_esm5, 1)` g/day, and each 0.1 kg of average infant
weight, which is not published per pair, moves it by about
`r round(rs_per_100g, 1)` g/day. Treat `Rs` computed from this model as
reproducing the paper to within about 10 g/day.

The paper's exclusive-breastfeeding cut-off of 86.6 g/day is the 90th
percentile of the *pooled individual posterior* distributions of the 113
pairs. It mixes each pair's estimation uncertainty (individual 95% credible
intervals with a median half-width of about 38 g/day, ESM 5) with the spread
of their shrunken posterior means, so it is a property of the fitted data set
rather than a quantile of the population model and is not compared here; the
90th percentile of the simulated between-pair `Rs` is
`r round(quantile(rs_pairs$Rs, 0.9), 1)` g/day.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error not reported.** The combined error model of the paper
  shares one (proportional, additive) pair between mother and infant, but the
  posterior values of `sigma` are not printed in the paper or in any
  supplement. Both pairs are held at zero, so simulations are of the true
  saliva enrichment; rxode2 needs a separate pair per endpoint, so the model
  carries `propSd`/`addSd` and `propSd_Cinfant`/`addSd_Cinfant`.
* **Unreported IIV correlations.** The paper fitted a full 4 x 4 LKJ
  correlation matrix but prints only the `CLmb`-`CLbo` correlation (0.99,
  ESM 7). The other five correlations are set to zero. In the ESM 5 individual
  posterior means they are small (between -0.13 and 0.24).
* **BSV reading.** Table S6.1's "BSV %" is taken as 100 x the log-scale SD,
  as ESM 7 states explicitly for `CLmb` and `CLbo` ("SD as Between Subject
  Variability", 0.20 and 0.17) and as the arithmetic-mean check above
  confirms for all four parameters.
* **kmm typical value back-solved.** No log-scale mean is printed for `kmm`;
  `lkel = log(0.109) - 0.15^2 / 2` from Table S6.1. The ESM 5 geometric mean,
  0.1071 1/day, agrees within 0.7%.
* **ODE instead of the closed form.** The Stan code evaluates the analytic
  solution with the infant volume frozen at each observation time; the
  packaged model integrates the mass-balanced ODEs with a time-varying infant
  volume. They are identical for constant infant weight and differ by up to
  about 1.7% at day 14 for typical growth (shown above).
* **Infant weight on CLbo.** The paper evaluates the infant-clearance
  covariate at the infant's average weight over the study (Stan `BWT`); the
  packaged model uses the current `WT_INFANT`. With 0.3 kg of growth on a 6 kg
  infant and an exponent of 0.17 this changes `CLbo` by less than 0.5% at any
  time; supply a constant `WT_INFANT` equal to the study average to remove
  even that, at the cost of a constant infant volume.
* **Rs reproduced only approximately.** See the `Rs` section: the model's
  population-mean `Rs` is `r round(rs_expected, 1)` g/day against the
  published 50.7 g/day, a gap of the size explained by the difference between
  the paper's own two summaries of the clearances and the unpublished infant
  weights.
* **Constants held at their prior means.** The Stan model samples the TBW
  coefficients `a` and `b`, the milk water fraction, the oxidation water
  fraction and the atmospheric absorption fraction from informative priors.
  The packaged model and the `Rs` calculation use the prior means.
* **Reference weights.** Eqs. 16-17 centre on 70 kg (mother) and 5 kg
  (infant), which the paper calls the median weights although Table 1 gives
  53.1 kg and 5.9 kg; the model uses 70 kg and 5 kg, as the fitted code does.
* **Virtual cohort.** Individual weights are not published. Maternal and
  start-of-study infant weights are drawn log-normally around the Table 1
  medians and redrawn when outside the Table 1 ranges; every infant gains the
  median 0.3 kg over 14 days, linearly, as the Stan code assumes.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found for this article (Europe
  PMC, checked 2026-11-25).
